newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Electrolux cleans up after closure decision.
newsitem.headline: Electrolux cleans up after closure decision.

text.p: The stock of Sweden's AB Electrolux, the world's largest supplier of household appliances, soared to record levels Friday after a tough restructuring programme was announced a day earlier.

New Chief Executive Michael Treschow stamped his mark on the appliance company, which owns the Frigidaire brand in the United States, with the surprise announcement of the two-year plan after just two months at the helm.

Treschow announced Electrolux would close about 25 of 150 plants and cut 12,000 staff from a workforce of 105,000 in a 2.5 billion crown ($321 million) programme that will be charged against second quarter earnings.

Electrolux's share price soared 64 crowns ($8.23) by Thursday's close after the news and gained 63 crowns on Friday to close at 592 crowns ($76.68) after hitting an all-time high of 600 crowns ($77.12) during the session.
Several analysts said Electrolux, long held back by concern over its performance in the highly competitive market for appliances such as refrigerators and washing machines, could go even higher.
U.S. investment bank Lehman Brothers analyst Chris Heminway said the firm added Electrolux to its European strategy "recommended" list due to its restructuring plan.

The turnaround in Electrolux's stock came on the same day that its main competitor Whirlpool issued a warning that European appliance sales were expected to decline again this year for the fifth year running.
Whirlpool predicted a one percent decline in appliance sales in Europe. "The environment (in Europe) is terribly negative," Whirlpool's European head Jeff Fettig told The Financial Times.

Analysts say the industry, which is characterised by mature markets, slow growth and extreme price pressure, is ripe for consolidation and it was high time for Electrolux to straighten out its balance sheet.
"Attention is very much going to be focused internally and that will give them a slight advantage in taking market share and therefore start the boat rocking," a Stockholm analyst said.

Treschow told Reuters Financial Television in an interview that there were signs of a turnaround in the crucial U.S. market, where competition for Electrolux' Frigidaire unit with Whirlpool is at its toughest.
"We have been losing money for some years on white goods (in the U.S.) but there are some encouraging signs. I'm rather optimistic that we are getting past the time of losing money there," he said.
